To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the papI gene is the mediator of thermosensing and transcriptional control of pap genes, that the PapI protein is a positive transcriptional regulator of the pap genes, that none of the other known pap proteins is involved in thermoregulation, that the rpoH gene is not required for thermoregulation and that the papI-pab intercistronic sequence is important in the thermoreduction of pap transcription.
the papI gene mediates temperature regulation at the transcriptional level, and that the PapI protein acts as a positive transcriptional regulator of pilus adhesion gene transcription.

the papI gene of a cloned uropathogenic Escherichia colipilus gene cluster encodes a transcription activator of the major pilin gene and other cistrons of the cluster and that the papI-pabB intercistron contains a determinant for the thermoregulatory control of pap transcription.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of the temperature-regulated expression of the pap gene cluster.
the molecular mechanism by which a bacterial cell regulates the synthesis of a surface protein.
the molecular mechanism of the temperature-dependent regulation of a virulence gene in Escherichia coil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PapI protein is the thermosensor and that the PapB protein is the thermomodulator, and that the PapA protein is the thermoreceptor.
the PapI activase is the mediator of the thermoregulated pap gene transcription.
the papI gene is the mediator of temperature regulation of pap gene transcription.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the papI gene encodes a positive regulator for the pap operon, that this regulation is mediated by a DNA-binding protein, and that the thermoregulatory function is due to a temperature-dependent change in the level of the PapI protein.
the PapI protein is a positive regulator of pilus adhesion genes and that its synthesis is thermoregulated by a mechanism which involves an intercistronic determinant in the papB-papI intercistron.
the papI gene encodes an activator that is required for pilus adhesions at all temperatures, but that its activity is temperature regulated at the level of mRNA accumulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of pilus adhesion is a multistep process, involving at least two transcriptional activators and a repressor.
the papI gene is a key element in the thermoregu- lated expression of the pap fimbrial adhesin.
thermoregulated expression of pilus adhesion genes is mediated by a transcriptional activator protein.
